neighbours.label: light verb ' take'/' took' and ' full' in take-idioms (take full advantage of, take care of)
fire: Members should take full advantage of the free parking this weekend.
Before the trip, please take care of the cat's food.
The students took full advantage of the extra study hall.
If you can, take care to lock the back gate tonight.
Shoppers will take full advantage of the holiday discount codes.
My brother promised to take care of the garden while I am away.
The team took full advantage of the opponent's mistakes.
Remember to take care when crossing the icy bridge.
quiet: Members should make good use of the free parking this weekend.
Before the trip, please feed the cat and fill its bowl.
The students made good use of the extra study hall.
If you can, remember to lock the back gate tonight.
Shoppers will happily use the holiday discount codes.
My brother promised to water the garden while I am away.
The team profited from the opponent's mistakes.
Remember to be careful when crossing the icy bridge.

notes: card: ' take' x6, ' full' x5, ' took' x4 among the top 32; probe: 'take full advantage' 0.55, 'take care' 0.44, 'made full use' 0.12.
